title: Low hot-water flow or pressure | G3 Cylinder Help
description: Understand low hot-water flow or pressure. Distinguish the symptom, gather useful details and arrange competent cylinder assessment in London.
answer: Weak delivery may involve the incoming water supply, inlet controls, restrictions or local outlets. Cylinder expansion is not a universal flow fix.

sections.heading: What this symptom can mean
paragraphs: Standing pressure and usable flow under demand are different measurements. One weak outlet suggests a different investigation from every hot tap becoming weak. An internal air-gap routine should not be sold as a guaranteed pressure upgrade.

sections.heading: Information to gather safely
paragraphs: Note whether cold outlets are also affected and what happens when more than one outlet runs. A competent assessment can separate supply limitations from a repairable restriction.

sections.heading: How the enquiry becomes an investigation
paragraphs: The cylinder make, full model and heating arrangement should be identified first. The same visible symptom can arise from different causes, and a relief device may be protecting the system rather than creating the original problem. Component testing and any repair belong to a person competent for the work.

sections.heading: Discuss the appropriate next step
paragraphs: Call 020 7205 4433 with the postcode, symptom history and any previous service findings. The enquiry establishes the proposed assessment and availability. Do not use this guide as a substitute for the actual appliance safety instructions or an on-site diagnosis.

faqs.question: Will replenishing a Megaflo air gap always increase shower flow?
faqs.answer: No. Expansion provision and outlet flow are different issues; supply, restrictions and shower controls need their own assessment.
